title: Queued confirmation executes while emergency stop remains active
observed: A genuine pending Level2 confirmation was created with a dummy tool. After kill_switch.trigger, active remained false; credentialed POST confirmation returned200 and invoked the dummy sink once. No shell ran.
boundary: The same authenticated operator later confirmed the action; no separate approver role or lower-trust privilege gain was established. Stock HTTP startup was not exercised.
fix: Enforce emergency-stop/revocation state at the common ToolRegistry dispatch boundary, invalidate pending approvals on stop, and bind each pending item to a short lifetime and revocation epoch. confirmed=True must satisfy the stop gate.
regression: Create pending dummy action, trigger stop, confirm it and assert zero dummy effects; repeat through native and HTTP dispatch.
resolution: Server/registry/getters refuse real effects and confirmation route is removed.

title: Streaming failure repeats an already completed tool effect
observed: One note_append input wrote one marker before a mocked Ollama failure. The exact stream-then-normal fallback wrote a second marker to the scratch-only note.
boundary: Demonstrated integrity/retry defect is a Level1 local note append in balanced mode. Level2 confirmation gates were not bypassed; no arbitrary command replay was demonstrated.
fix: Return a distinct already-executed/tool-result state from _process_stream. Reuse that result when narration fails rather than redispatching the tool. Preserve one logical operation identity across retry/fallback.
regression: Make narration fail after a dummy append, enter fallback and assert one append with both WebSocket and voice callers.
resolution: Server/registry/getters refuse real effects and confirmation route is removed.

title: Shutdown selects and terminates an unrelated same-UID process
observed: One harmless child outside the project, with inert app.main:app argv, was classified fastapi_server and terminated by genuine discovery/termination helpers. Every other PID was excluded inside the isolated PID namespace.
boundary: This violates the CLI JARVIS-owned resource scope. The operator already controlled the same-UID child; no lower-trust authority gain, arbitrary PID selection or remote privilege escalation was established.
fix: Track processes actually launched by JARVIS with PID plus creation time and verified executable/project provenance, and revalidate immediately before signalling. Reject a generic command-line marker as sufficient ownership.
regression: Run one owned dummy child and one unrelated same-entrypoint dummy child; shutdown must stop only the tracked owned child and tolerate PID reuse.
resolution: Final packaged source adds native child leases, bounded/cancellable VAD, validated/finally-cleaned /ws and authenticated CLI POST with explicit offline/failure policy; see eight selected packaged safety checks. D5 /ws is fixed; /ue5 sibling cleanup is separately retained as D7.

title: Continuous speech bypasses recording frame cap
observed: A finite fake stream supplied41 speech frames and1 silence frame. The genuine recorder returned42 frames (1.26s encoded audio) against a configured20-frame/0.6s cap, using40364 WAV bytes. This is encoded duration, not wall time.
boundary: The fixture establishes cap failure and source shows unbounded callback queues/weak active-recording cancellation. It does not establish a shared-service outage or physical audio attack.
fix: Check absolute monotonic deadline, frame budget and cancellation on every iteration before the speech continue; bound callback queues and avoid retaining an outer wake-listener backlog during nested capture.
regression: Use finite continuous-positive VAD input exceeding a small cap and assert recording ends at the cap; cancel during active capture and assert prompt exit with bounded queues.
resolution: Final packaged source adds native child leases, bounded/cancellable VAD, validated/finally-cleaned /ws and authenticated CLI POST with explicit offline/failure policy; see eight selected packaged safety checks. D5 /ws is fixed; /ue5 sibling cleanup is separately retained as D7.

title: Malformed accepted WebSocket sessions retain manager entries
observed: Three in-memory credentialed sessions: [] raised AttributeError and retained1 entry; a nonstring message raised TypeError and retained1; normal disconnect retained0.
boundary: This proves per-session parsing/cleanup defects. No connection flood, shared-service denial or authentication bypass was demonstrated; normal later broadcast may remove dead sockets.
fix: Validate incoming object/message type and size before processing. Always remove the connection in finally for disconnect, malformed input, exception and cancellation; add explicit connection/send limits.
regression: Submit nonobject/nonstring JSON and cancel a session; assert a defined close/error and an empty manager after each session.
resolution: Final packaged source adds native child leases, bounded/cancellable VAD, validated/finally-cleaned /ws and authenticated CLI POST with explicit offline/failure policy; see eight selected packaged safety checks. D5 /ws is fixed; /ue5 sibling cleanup is separately retained as D7.

title: CLI POST omits credential and treats HTTP failure as offline
observed: A configured dummy token was present, but the mocked CLI POST had no Authorization header. Its mocked401 led to the local light-sleep fallback.
boundary: The local same-UID operator is trusted, so this is not an HTTP authentication bypass. It can silently choose a different resource-control path than the active server.
fix: Use one authenticated GET/POST helper. Distinguish authentication/authorization failures from transport absence and require explicit handling before local fallback.
regression: Verify Bearer on POST;401/403 must report failure without invoking the local resource manager, while genuine offline handling remains explicit.
resolution: Final packaged source adds native child leases, bounded/cancellable VAD, validated/finally-cleaned /ws and authenticated CLI POST with explicit offline/failure policy; see eight selected packaged safety checks. D5 /ws is fixed; /ue5 sibling cleanup is separately retained as D7.
